correctness.rationale: Exact hub-first mixture, cycle-to-path first-vertex reduction, first/second factorial moment generating-function ODEs, and coefficient asymptotics establish the finite law and variance. The known one-dimensional path CLT gives the weak wheel normal limit. Factorial decay of decreasing-priority paths gives a fourth central moment O(n^2 log^2 n), strong enough for the o(1/n) lower-tail control and o(n^2) cycle third moment. Substitution into exact mixture moment identities establishes the sharp rare tail and divergent skewness. Independent exact-rational finite checks passed 62 assertions; they do not certify the infinite claims.

value.rationale: Wheels are a canonical natural graph family with a single diverging-degree hub and bounded-degree ring. Their rare-branching event shows that the ordinary one-dimensional Gaussian fluctuation theorem gives misleading variance and extreme-tail information on a minimally altered graph. The full finite law, sharp left tail, variance inflation, and growing skewness expose a mathematically meaningful boundary, rather than an arbitrary numerical coefficient.
